$comment: Tests RFC-AITP-0005 §9.4 (verifier-side Manifest expiry bound). The TCT's expires_at is in the future relative to the reference clock — the only failure is that it exceeds the issuing peer's Manifest expires_at. The verifier MUST reject with TCT_EXPIRES_AFTER_MANIFEST, NOT the generic TCT_EXPIRED (see tct-002 for the literal-expiry case). Folding both cases into one code hides 'TCT outlived its issuer's credential' behind 'TCT past its own deadline.'
description: A TCT whose `expires_at` is after the issuing peer's Manifest `expires_at` MUST be rejected with `TCT_EXPIRES_AFTER_MANIFEST` (RFC-AITP-0005 §9.4; issuer-side constraint is RFC-AITP-0004 §4.3). The TCT itself is not expired (`expires_at` is in the future), signature/audience/cnf are otherwise valid, and the issuer's Manifest is supplied via `input.issuer_manifest` so the §9.4 conditional check fires. Verifiers that fold this case into the generic `TCT_EXPIRED` lose the ability to distinguish 'TCT outlived its issuer's credential' from 'TCT past its own deadline.'

expected.rationale: tct.expires_at (__NOW_PLUS_7200__) > issuer_manifest.expires_at (__NOW_PLUS_3600__). The §9.4 bound is violated even though the TCT itself is not yet expired. The TCT_EXPIRED code is reserved for the literal-expiry case (tct-002).
